newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican diplomat sees Iran's foreign minister.
newsitem.headline: Vatican diplomat sees Iran's foreign minister.

text.p: The Vatican's top diplomat, Secretary of State Cardinal Angelo Sodano, has discussed freedom of religion in Iran with the country's Foreign Minister, Ali Akbar Velayati, a Vatican spokesman said on Wednesday.
Sodano received Velayati, who is on a visit to Italy, at the Vatican on Tuesday, chief Vatican spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls said in a statement.
"During the course of the meeting, they reviewed relations between the Vatican and Iran, in particular the issue of freedom of the various religions present in Iran," Navarro-Valls said.
He said they also exchanged views on the problems of the Middle East peace process.
Moslem Iran has diplomatic ties with the Vatican.
An Iranian anti-government group, the National Council of Iranian Resistance, criticised Sodano for receiving Velayati.

"It comes at a time in which Christians find themselves under maximum pressure in Iran and several Christian leaders have been brutally assassinated by mercenaries of the regime," the group said in a statement issued in Rome.
Velayati met Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Wednesday. No details of their discussion were made public.

Velayati met his Italian counterpart Lamberto Dini on Tuesday evening. A ministry statement said Dini told the Iranian that he hoped Iran would increasingly distance itself from what he called international terrorism.
Dini also said Italy intended to continue along the route of "critical dialogue" begun by the European Union "to favour the gradual reintegration of (Iran) in international relations".

Europe's position contrasts with that of the United States, which has urged the international community to isolate Iran, contending it sponsors terrorism and plays host to Islamic fundamentalists bent on destabilising governments in North Africa and the Middle East.
